name: Reviewer fit for an AI control research sprint track (hypothetical)
brief: A weekend research sprint with three technical tracks: control setting design (new evaluation environments for testing control protocols), control protocol design (monitors, defer-to-trusted strategies, auditing budgets) and red-teaming (attack policies that evade trusted monitors). Reviewers read 5 to 8 submissions each in the week after the event, score them on impact, execution and presentation, and write a short rationale. The panel needs people who have read control papers, not general ML seniority.

criteria.name: Direct experience in the track's research area
criteria.description: Published, built or worked on control, monitoring, evaluations or red-teaming of language-model agents. General machine-learning seniority does not pass this gate.

criteria.name: Available for 2 to 3 hours in the review week
criteria.description: Stated availability for the week after the event. Over-committed candidates (several conferences the same week) fail this gate.

criteria.name: Seniority tier
criteria.description: Senior (5+ years, leads work, established publications) can take the ambiguous submissions; mid (2 to 5 years, active researcher) takes standard technical evaluations; junior (PhD or early) takes focused technical assessments only.

anchors.5: Senior: leads a research group or has a publication record in the area.
anchors.3: Mid: active researcher with specialised expertise.
anchors.1: Junior: specific technical skills, no evaluation experience yet.

criteria.name: Has evaluated other people's research before
criteria.description: Peer review, programme committees, grant review, judging, mentoring research projects.

anchors.5: Regular reviewer or committee member in the field.
anchors.3: Has reviewed a few times or mentored research.

criteria.name: Identity and claims verified from a second source
criteria.description: A personal site, scholar profile, lab page or alumni page confirms the claims. Weak LinkedIn presence is normal for safety researchers and is not evidence against.

anchors.5: Two independent sources confirm role and publications.
anchors.1: Nothing found; request a CV before confirming.

criteria.name: Low conflict-of-interest risk
criteria.description: Not at the same organisation as several submitting teams, not a co-organiser's direct report. Score high when no overlap is visible.

anchors.3: One possible overlap, handled by exclusion.

notes: Keynote-tier people get a speaking invitation, not an asynchronous reviewing request; put them in a different pipeline. Never oversell the batch: a reviewer who withdraws over submission quality was a fit mistake on our side. Once a person is told they are on the panel, they are on the panel; control the assignment instead of retracting.
